Subject: Private VPC deployment - recap & next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Emily & Austin — great conversation. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can line up the right deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC):

Call highlights:
- FinTechCo is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment due to regulatory requirements and data residency (transaction metadata must remain in your VPC).
- Primary integration pattern: API calls from your app servers (in us-west-2) to a PrivateLink endpoint or VPC peering into Redwood-managed nodes.
- Non-negotiables: IP allowlist for management plane access, SOC 2 evidence for dedicated/private, and KMS integration for keys.
- Expected volume: ~5M inference tokens/month initially with burst patterns during end-of-month reconciliation.

Questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Networking options: PrivateLink vs VPC peering — rough pros/cons for latency and egress costs.
2) IP allowlist: static outbound IPs we can use for webhook callbacks and metrics.
3) Deployment topology: single AZ vs multi-AZ, and whether dedicated capacity or private on-prem is required for compliance.

Next steps (proposed):
- Sean (cc) to share a short networking checklist + expected IP ranges for PrivateLink and peering.
- Redwood to share the Private VPC checklist PDF and a simple peering diagram (attached).
- FinTechCo to confirm desired topology (single AZ vs multi-AZ) and any procurement timelines by next Wednesday (2027-03-10).

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (checklist), vpc-peering-diagram.png (topology sketch).

If that all looks right I can schedule a quick 30-min follow-up with Sean to walk the infra team through the technical bits.

Thanks Emily — great context. Looping in Sean and Jonas from our infra team to address the specific networking and IP questions. See quick answers below; happy to jump on a screenshare to walk the network team through details.

Sean / Jonas — summary and requests from FinTechCo:
- Preference: PrivateLink if latency is acceptable (FinTechCo target: <100ms for fraud path).
- Topology: start POC single-AZ then promote to multi-AZ for production.
- Needs: static IPs or well-known NAT endpoints for allowlisting, confirm egress/cost differences, and KMS integration details.

Sean, preliminary notes you can use in the call:
- PrivateLink vs VPC peering: PrivateLink keeps traffic on AWS backbone and avoids public internet hops, typically simplifies security posture (no route table changes in customer VPC). Latency is usually comparable to peering for intra-region; we'll validate with a short perf test.
- IP allowlist: for management/control plane, we provide a set of static egress IP ranges (see checklist). For the data plane, PrivateLink creates ENIs in the customer VPC so traffic originates from customer VPC, eliminating the need to open inbound from our side except for management.
- Egress/cost: Peering may incur cross-AZ data transfer costs depending on topology; PrivateLink has interface endpoint hourly and data processing costs but often reduces egress because traffic stays within the AWS network for the customer. We'll share an exemplar cost comparison for your expected volume.

Jonas, can you attach the short JSON/YAML snippet we send to customers for peering CIDR and the sample security group rules? Also please confirm the specific IP ranges we recommend for management plane allowlist.

Emily / Austin — I propose a 30-min technical call next Tue 2027-03-09 at 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include a perf test script we can run during the POC.
